Semantics old vs new: old OMS = not contains Mostrador (PicapAutoAcceptPolicy.kt line 119 before diff), so blank servicio and every non-Mostrador label matched. New OMS = contains cruz verde AND (integracion OR integracion-acute), ignoreCase (PicapParser.kt lines 72-75). Orders that leave OMS and match only TODOS now: any non-blank Cruz Verde label without Integracion plus blank servicio orders. Nothing broader: Mostrador-only labels stay non-OMS.

Accent/case matrix executed against the real kotlin-stdlib StringsKt.contains with ignoreCase true: Cruz Verde Integracion true; Cruz Verde Integracion-acute true; fully uppercase accented true; blank false; Cruz Verde Mostrador false. Case folding folds acute forms correctly.
Only accent representation that misses: decomposed NFD (o + combining acute) matches neither literal, so isOmsService returns false. Kotlin and Java never Unicode-normalize on read.
Token conjunction is order-agnostic: reversed Integracion-acute plus Cruz Verde still true.

Address false-positive path: PicapParser.parseOrder lines 56-60 sets servicio to the first text containing cruz verde that is not exactly equal to dirRec or dirEnt, so captured direction lines never reach isOmsService; even if a direction line became servicio it would still need integracion to be OMS, strictly lower false-positive risk than the old rule.

Blank servicio never reaches the policy in the auto-accept flow: PicapOfferProcessor.kt lines 243-257 rejects empty-servicio offers with an Aceptar node as NO-CRUZ-VERDE and returns before shouldAutoAccept (call site line 263), so blank to TODOS-only is consistent with the existing product rule.

Grep of app/src/main for OMS and Mostrador: no other code still classifies OMS with the old rule. findings.claim: The accent handling is case-insensitive but not Unicode-normalization-safe: a decomposed NFD service label such as Integracion written with a combining acute matches neither the unaccented nor the precomposed literal, so a genuine Cruz Verde Integracion order would silently stop matching filter OMS and drop to TODOS only. All case and accent variants the intent calls for, including fully uppercase accented, do match; NFD is the only representation gap and it is new because the diff introduced accent-sensitive literals into a rule that previously only checked Mostrador.
proof_refs: stdlib probe: NFD false, NFC true, fully uppercase accented true

findings.claim: OMS and MOSTRADOR are no longer mutually exclusive. The old OMS rule guaranteed disjointness; the new branch does not exclude Mostrador, so a service text containing both Cruz Verde Integracion and Mostrador would satisfy both filters, while the card still labels it Mostrador because OrderCard checks Mostrador before isOmsService. A user filtering by OMS could therefore accept and display an order whose card title says Mostrador. Trigger requires a dual-token label, so impact is likely nil in practice, but the loss of the disjoint invariant is a real side effect of the diff and is not documented in the updated KDoc.

The new public business rule isOmsService has no automated coverage. It is a pure, trivially unit-testable function whose accent and case matrix is subtle, yet the diff adds it with only the pre-existing example stub tests in the project, so any future edit to the literals or to ignoreCase would regress silently and unobserved.
